title: Contextual Benchmarks Scratchpad
content:
Goal: quick, noisy consolidation of papers + threads I want to convert into reproducible micro-benchmarks for the long-context pipeline. Mostly notes to self — messy.

Top takeaways (sketch):
- KV-compression papers: several approaches (product quantization on keys, learned projection + residuals) — low-rank & PQ combo looks promising for 2–4x memory without big accuracy loss on retrieval tasks (see arXiv 2303.00045).
- Prompt caching vs KV caching: for our chat workloads, prefix reuse is high for system+instruction tokens but user tokens vary; need hybrid eviction policy (LRU for high-entropy user tokens, frequency for system).
- Flash-attention variants: important for piecewise long windows; pairing with chunked KV eviction reduces p95 by ~10–15% in prior notes.

Immediate experiments to spin up:
- [ ] Small kv-compress eval: run baseline (no compression) + quant-keys (int8 asymmetric) + PQ(4x8) on 7B model traces. Measure: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, end-to-end memory, and perplexity on heldout prompt set. (Ticket: RWD-4821 — link above)
- [ ] Cache eviction A/B: implement hybrid policy in local replay harness (use 10k sessions sample). Metrics: hit-rate by token position, effective latency, cost-per-token estimate.
- [ ] Long-window evals with mixed kernels: run sequence lengths {2k,8k,32k} with Flash-A + chunked KV to see kernel switching overheads.

Notes from papers / links to read fully:
- arXiv 2303.00045 — PQ + low-rank on KV; skimmed the evals, they do QA + retrieval re-rank. Need to check prompt formatting differences.
- Blog: "Trading tokens for memory" — good intuition on eviction thresholds; experiment idea: use RL-ish controller to decide eviction budget per session.
- MoE-inference notes: gating overhead kills latency if we shard across hosts; for dedicated we can test single-host MoE with local routing.

Preliminary hypotheses:
1) PQ on keys will yield ~1.8–2.5x memory reduction with <1.5% relative generation quality drop if we keep float values for values and only compress keys.
2) Hybrid eviction (freq/system affinity) will preserve effective cached prefix hit-rate for convo systems where assistant prompts repeat common templates.
3) Kernel switching (optimized compile-time selection) matters more than raw kernel throughput when sequences are heterogeneous; op-level overhead dominates at <50ms window durations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What does "quality" mean for downstream user metrics? BLEU/perplexity is fine for quick checks but need to set a UX-aligned metric (edit distance on retrieval snippets? rate of hallucination?).
- Should we add a small synthetic workload that injects repeated system+instruction tokens to stress prefix caching and measure worst-case cache growth?
- Who to sync with: Lina for cache harness, Kai for kernel/compile changes, SRE for memory headroom.

Useful commands / quick notes to self:
- Local harness: ./bench/run_replay --trace traces/2026-05-sampled.json --model 7b --kv-compress pq4x8 --eviction hybrid
- Quick eval scoring: python scoring/compare_gen.py --ref data/longform-dev.json --pred outputs/*.json --metrics ppl,bleu,edit_ratio

Slack crumbs: asked @lina about replay traces (she said yes, will drop in #bench-traces). Left VM note to bump swap off for stable mem numbers.

Next steps (this week):
- finalize small bench config + baseline runs (by Wed 2026-06-03)
- write a short explainer doc for Eng-runbook that summarizes results and recommended knob values (QPS vs compression tradeoffs).

Random scribbles:
- If PQ meets expectations, try a layered cache: hot prefix -> compressed key store -> cold deep store (LRU compaction every N minutes).
- Could piggyback model-quant metadata in routing policy so we fallback to higher-precision variant if evictions cause quality drop.

End of scratchpad — will refine into a proper doc after first run.
